content.thinking:
I need to implement `canViewProject` and enforce it in the relevant areas.

`canViewProject` must guard project lookups, issue and comment writes, and listings. Lookups throw `NotFoundError`. Writes targetting the project or its contents also throw `NotFoundError` and change nothing. Listings silently exclude hidden projects and issues, and their counts reflect only visible items. Membership and lead changes take effect immediately. Search is out of scope.
The task requires building a project list and an org-wide issue list.

Private projects the actor cannot view must be excluded from listings.

The `canViewProject` check will filter out private projects by verifying platform staff status, org admin or owner role, lead identity, and membership. Totals must remain accurate.

Visibility checks will be added to services. Listings will be filtered by loading all projects.

Pagination is the main challenge. Hidden items could occupy slots and break totals. The plan is to fetch all private projects in the org, compute hidden IDs, and filter SQL with notInArray. Optional excludeProjectIds will be added to repository functions.

The optional excludeIds argument will be internal-only so existing callers remain valid. Issue lists will return an empty page with total 0 when a hidden project is requested, rather than throwing NotFound.

Even when a specific projectId is requested, hidden projects will be silently omitted and return an empty page with total 0. This prevents leaking information about a project's existence through error type differences.

A new `assertProjectVisible` helper will throw NotFoundError for private projects. It will be used in project-service, issue-service, comment-service, and attachment-service.

Labels are org-wide, not project-scoped.

Adding optional exclude filters to repository lists. A helper will collect hidden project IDs. A new `listProjectsByVisibility` repository function is cleaner than querying all projects with a high limit.

Optional parameters keep existing tests passing. The service layer will pass hidden project IDs into the repository list query, using a Drizzle `notInArray` filter guarded against empty arrays. A new helper is being drafted to efficiently collect inaccessible private project IDs.

The drafted helper fetches up to 1000 projects and filters them manually. That limit risks missing projects. A dedicated repository query is preferable.

A dedicated `findProjectsByVisibility` repository method will handle visibility filtering. Unpaged queries are rejected to keep services decoupled from direct database access. Leads, admins, owners, and staff can view private projects without membership.

Role checks will use `hasRoleAtLeast` instead of direct string comparisons. Membership and lead status are verified on every call rather than cached. Hidden projects will throw a NotFoundError with the same "Project" entity name and ID as missing projects.

NotFoundError entity names are being aligned with the lookup context. Issues and comment threads will report "Issue" not found. Boards will report "Project" not found. Comment edits and deletions will report "Comment" not found, though this risks leaking that the comment exists.

The NotFoundError entity name will match the specific resource the caller requested. Project operations report "Project" not found, issue operations report "Issue" not found, and creating an issue reports "Project" not found because the target is the project.

The visibility check must run before `assertCan` to prevent leaking permission errors. If the parent project is not viewable, the operation throws `NotFoundError` immediately after loading the entity. This ensures members without permission see `Forbidden`, while outsiders see `NotFound`.

`canViewProject` only checks visibility rules and does not validate organization scope. Cross-organization access is handled by `assertOrgScope` before this check runs.

Admin, owner, lead, and member checks will require the actor's organization ID to match the project's organization ID. Platform staff remain exempt from this restriction.

Visibility filtering will apply to both org-wide issue lists and project lists.

Project-scoped issue lists will silently omit hidden projects and return an empty page with total zero. The `listIssues` function will append the visibility exclusion directly in its query rather than modifying `issueFilters`.

Adding an optional `exclude` argument to the repository call so direct callers still see all issues. Search reindex should index private projects, and search results remain unfiltered.

Exclusion logic will live only in the service list path. A shared `canViewProject` helper will be added to project-service and reused by issue-service. Comment-service will also import it. No circular imports are expected.

`assertProjectVisible` will throw a `NotFoundError` when the actor cannot view the project. For issues, callers will check visibility and throw their own error instead. An `assertIssueVisible` helper is being drafted to verify the issue's parent project is accessible.

`assertCommentVisible` will verify the comment's parent issue exists and its project is accessible. `getThread` throws `NotFoundError` for a missing issue. `createIssue` throws `NotFoundError` for a missing project before any insert. Visibility checks may run before archive checks.

Visibility checks will run immediately after loading a resource, before archive or permission checks. This prevents leaking whether an item is archived when it is simply inaccessible. A `listProjectsWithVisibility` helper will be added to fetch projects by visibility level.

Archived private projects will be excluded from includeArchived lists. A `projectIdsHiddenFrom` helper is being drafted to return project IDs that an actor cannot view, with platform staff and org admins bypassing the check.

The `projectIdsHiddenFrom` helper will iterate over private projects and collect IDs the actor cannot view. The early return for admins is an optimization, since `canViewProject` already returns true for them. Members who are leads of private projects must still be checked individually. `projectIdsHiddenFrom` will remain in project-service and be exported for issue-service to use.

`projectIdsHiddenFrom` will be exported as a named function for issue-service to import. Both repositories need the `notInArray` import. Cursor pagination stays consistent because excluded rows are omitted from the result set.

Comment visibility checks will run before permission and edit-window validations. Attachment writes will be blocked when the parent project is inaccessible, since attachments are part of the project. Internal attachment lookups during deletion will also respect visibility, failing with NotFound if the attachment's issue sits in a hidden project.

Visibility checks will run after finding an issue in `findAttachment` so deletion fails cleanly. `listAttachments` will throw `NotFoundError` for a missing issue. `moveIssue` routes through `changeIssueStatus`. Comments on hidden issues will return `NotFoundError` before rate-limit consumption to avoid side effects. Activity lists are out of scope.
